decisions.reason: The message's splash-control changes are already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; the stronger mixing-quality target requires no additional state change.
The unresolved whisk material and style question is already represented by the same-message AMBIGUOUS Event; the mixing-quality update does not establish an additional whisk design value.
A stronger, frothier mixing target does not necessarily change the selected 4.5 qt capacity, bowl depth, or accepted refilling behavior.
The message's new dispensing requirements are already captured by the candidate's same-message MODIFY, while its prior preservation, dripping, and flow constraints remain valid.
The mixing-texture target and question about motor speed do not change the requirement to use standard 120V wall power.
The source changes the desired mixing result but does not change the required wiring-plan deliverable or its level of detail.
The client expressly retains the solenoid approach, so the existing solenoid and press-to-pour control state remains unchanged.
The effective-sealing statement reiterates the existing requirement to prevent liquid from entering the base and electronics without materially changing it.
The request for removable or easily cleaned spout components restates the existing removal-or-easy-flushing cleanability requirement.
The optional cleaning statement does not alter the existing requirement for easy bowl removal and rapid event-time swapping.
The mixing-quality decision does not affect the placard text, position, or customer-facing orientation.
The stronger and smoother mixing target does not necessarily change the enclosure's size constraint or side-profile proportions.
